chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Ayoub ibn Atiyya Al-Hazza', who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) distributed the Fay (booty/wealth), and Ali (peace be upon him) was assigned a piece of land. He dug a well in it, and water gushed out towards the sky in the form of a camel's neck. So he named it 'Yanbu' (the gusher).

The herald of good news came with the good news, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Give the good news to the inheritors. It is a charity, irrevocable, for the pilgrims of the House of Allah and the passers-by in the Way of Allah. It shall not be sold, nor gifted, nor inherited.'
So whoever sells it or gifts it, upon him is the Curse of Allah, the Angels, and all people. Allah will not accept from him any exchange or ransom.

key_terms.لَا تُبَاعُ وَ لَا تُوهَبُ وَ لَا تُورَث: Not sold, not gifted, and not inherited

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling or gifting the Prophet's charity land according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the unique status of Imam Ali’s (as) land grant as an irrevocable charity (*sadaqah khalidah*) for the benefit of pilgrims and travelers, emphasizing its perpetual nature distinct from ordinary property. The Prophet’s declaration that it 'cannot be sold, gifted, or inherited' establishes a legal precedent for *waqf* in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring the asset remains dedicated to public utility. The severe curse upon those who alter its status underscores the sanctity of preserving charitable endowments for the sake of Allah.
